ruleInterpretations: Simultaneously means each selected participant commits privately without seeing earlier choices. Participant membership and its original in-range qualification freeze at the accepted activation. No draw, entitlement or revealed vote is published until all commitments exist.

Each option-2 participant causes one actual owner draw. An option-1 participant may be selected as an extra target for each Slash during this actual Play phase. If all participants agree, each also executes the other option: owner draws their number of cards and every participant receives extra-target eligibility. The one-participant case is therefore unanimous.

The text grants an extra target, without an unlimited-distance clause. This implementation infers that ordinary current Slash target requirements still apply when appending: current range, directed/suit/card prohibition, living state, exclusion of the user and existing targets. Initial in-range membership does not permanently bypass distance after a weapon or distance change.

The text says 本阶段 rather than while the skill is present. Issued eligibility persists after source loss through that actual Play phase, then expires; an accepted Slash freezes its issued grants before its native payment children. An owner death does not undo a completed draw or already-issued fact, but offers no further dead-player choices.

No official FAQ was found establishing a different simultaneous tie, later range, or source-loss rule. These temporal and continuation details are explicit implementation inferences, not separately quoted official rulings.
runtimeBoundaries: Private votes, participant order, draw receipt and target draft live on the original ProgramSkillFrame. The native CardUseFrame owns its immutable phase-grant receipt before payment.
Persistent phase grants and provenance use scalar facts, without a mutable pending sidecar. Native draw movements and all their real observer/damage/rescue children drain once through typed returns.
Native Slash target cursor, responses, damage and producer returns are preserved; additional targets never rewrite a zero-entity producer's original single primary selection.
